title: Krishna in Mathura
body:
Krishna in Mathura

After his many failures, Kansa sent his chief minister Akroora to Vrindavan to invite Krishna and Balarama to Mathura, ostensibly to take part in a Danur-Yagna and a wrestling competition, but in truth intending to have them killed there. Akroora conveyed the king's invitation to Nanda and Yashoda, and though Yashoda was firmly against sending Krishna, He was resolved to go, and accepted. They set out the next morning, and by evening halted to rest by the banks of the Yamuna. As Akroora took his ritual dip, a vision unfolded before him: he beheld Lord Vishnu in Vaikuntham with Goddess Lakshmi at His side, and then saw the Lord's form become Krishna and Balarama. In that moment Akroora understood the divine purpose behind the journey.
Reaching Mathura, Krishna and Balarama dismounted at the city gates, wishing to see the city before the competition, and sent Akroora ahead to announce their arrival. As they walked the streets, Krishna performed His first miracle in the city. A deformed woman named Trivakra, bent with a severe hunchback, fell at His feet; Krishna placed the sole of His foot upon hers, and as He gently lifted her, her deformities vanished and her spine straightened, transforming her into a beautiful maiden. Overwhelmed with gratitude, she offered to guide them through Mathura, and led them to the arena where the Danur-Yagna was taking place. There Krishna walked to the great bow at the center of the hall, lifted it single-handedly, strung it, and snapped it in two, the crack echoing across the stadium and leaving the crowd stunned.
Seeing his plan to intimidate Krishna fail, Kansa devised another. That night he ordered the keeper of his mightiest elephant, Koliyapeed, to intoxicate the beast and loose it upon Krishna and Balarama the next morning. As the drunken elephant charged through the streets, Balarama seized it by the tail, spun it about, and hurled it high into the air, so that it came crashing down into the arena, dead upon impact. Krishna and Balarama then entered the wrestling contest and defeated Kansa's mightiest wrestlers, the brothers Chanura and Mushtika. At last, seeing his champions fallen, Kansa was forced to face Krishna himself, but he proved no match; Krishna swiftly overpowered and slew him, ending his reign of tyranny. With Kansa dead, the people of Mathura rejoiced, and Krishna freed His parents, Vasudeva and Devaki, along with His grandfather King Ugrasena, who had long languished in prison. Righteousness restored, a new era began for the kingdom.
